title: Astra-6 and other AI Worksflows
author: Nice-Investigator424
selftext:
Wanted to hear from people who are seeing success what their current workflows are using AI for game dev. 

I am just getting started and struggling to get a consistent workflow for 3D design and rigging

Appreciate your feedback!!!

comments.author: CaptainAlexWest
comments.body:
Astra is being potato right now. 

You can computer use and mcp in blender.

My current workflow on anything is.

Figure out what to build in the current project.

Build a block then fix bugs then commit.

Then repeat. 

Hopefully after 1000 blocks. I have a real game.

I used ai chat to figure out the prompts and what next moves to do in the project.

The micro context makes my brain hurt.

comments.author: doudou262
comments.body:
Rigging is where most AI workflows break down, so you are not alone there.

What seems to work for folks is splitting it: use AI for fast concept art and blockout meshes to explore ideas, then do retopology and rigging by hand in Blender where consistency matters. Keep your AI prompts and seeds saved so you can iterate on the same character.

Nail one small character end to end first. That loop teaches more than any tool list.

replies.author: Nice-Investigator424
replies.body:
That makes a lot of sense, thank you

Some I’ve been doing is use generic AI for concept art, then use Tripo for creating the mesh (they have an option for creating a clean mesh) then use Astra for texturing, rigging, etc.

comments.author: Legitimate-Paint2165
comments.body: Sol set to high with access to GitHub for everything. Astray only when needed with Sol generated prompts. I can get features built while at work and playtest when I get home.

replies.author: Nice-Investigator424
replies.body: What do you do when it comes to 3d modeling? Has that been with Sol as well?

replies.author: Legitimate-Paint2165
replies.body: I've done Blender MCP with Astra. Others have had better results than me. I suggest using Mixamo for rigging humanoids.

comments.author: OrphanNode
comments.body:
I built a pipeline for my game. I'll take a piece of concept art and upload it to have it trace dimension, then based on my game specifically, it will choose a style contract to apply to it and go through a few interations of creating a dimensioning file to import into blender, use the playwrite extension to snap a picture, judge the model, reiterate, until it comes to me for review. Mind you my game style isn't the most artistically detailed models out there. 

The rigging is a bit of a pain for character movement, but I also just have my character being a robot on tracks with noodle arms to alleviate some of the tension.
